service.description: Start an import of a GitHub repository (sourceRepository, owner/name) into a group (groupId), by the group's Owner with a confirmed address or an operator: into a repository of the group (repositoryId; one with issues or merge requests the import did not make is refused, numbersTaken, since numbers are kept) or a new one (slug, as wide as the group). token, a GitHub token that may read the repository, is kept encrypted for the run and dropped when it ends. options: issues and pullRequests (both by default). GitHub is asked for the repository now: sourceRefused (Unprocessable) when it refuses the token or has no such repository. Conflict (importActive) while a run of the same source or into the same repository is active. The run then goes a step at a time (run#Import). Creates take operationId.

An import as its group's Owners and operators see it: its repository and source, its stage (queued, labels, issues, pulls, comments, links, done, failed, cancelled), counts by type (imported, source: seen at GitHub, failed), what could not be carried (reportList: sourceType, sourceId, errorText; notCarried: what is never carried, and reactions the forum does not have, by kind), waitingUntil while GitHub's rate limit holds it, running while a step runs, and revision.
The imports into a group (groupId), for its Owners, newest first, paged; with no group, every import of the site, for an operator.

Go on with a failed or cancelled import from where it stopped, or give a running one another token (token; needed once a run ended, since its token was dropped), with expectedRevision. Conflict while a step runs; notAvailable for a done import (start it again: what it has is not made twice, and what failed is tried again).
Stop an import where it is, with expectedRevision; its token is dropped. What it made stays, and it can be resumed with a token.

A repository's push mirrors, for its Maintainers: the address, the refs, whether it deletes refs the repository no longer has, enabled, hasCredential (never the credential), the last push, its result and error, and the next attempt. notBuilt until the framework has push mirrors (F6).

Make a push mirror (operationId) or change one (mirrorId), by a Maintainer with a confirmed address: url (https, with no credential in it), username and secret (a token; write-only), hostKeyFingerprint, refs (ref patterns, comma separated), deleteRefs, enabled. Unprocessable for an address the framework's outbound rules refuse. notBuilt until the framework has push mirrors (F6).
Remove a push mirror, by a Maintainer. notBuilt until the framework has push mirrors (F6).

Push a mirror now, by a Maintainer: queued. Conflict while a push of it runs. The framework's outbound check holds the pushes of a hidden repository. notBuilt until the framework has push mirrors (F6).

A step of an import, as the account that started it (another account's call does nothing): at most budget API requests (10) from where its cursor is, each source item written in a transaction of its own, and the cursor saved. Nothing while GitHub's rate limit holds the run (waitingUntil) or while another step runs. The account must still own the group, else the run fails. Answers the stage, waitingUntil, the requests made and done once the run ended.

actions.script: const out = ec.resource.script("component://mr-mantle/service/mantle/smithy/Smithy.js").runImport({importId, budget}) stage = out.stage || null waitingUntil = out.waitingUntil || null requests = out.requests || 0 done = !!out.done

service.description: For the smithy_run_imports job: a step of each import that is due, as the account that started it (logged in without a password for the step); one whose account is gone fails. Each stands alone.
For the SmithyClaimGithubPlaceholder rule (entity/Smithy.eecas.xml): after the commit of the account, in a transaction of its own, claim#GithubAccount. Never fails the write: a failure is logged.

An account whose sign-in through a GitHub provider (an OauthFlow of type OctGitHub) linked a GitHub id (UserAccount.externalUserId) claims, in each site, the import's placeholder of that id: the account takes its GitHub login (SmithyAccount.githubLogin and githubUserId, so the agreement counts its imported commits) and its posts, issues, merge requests, assignments and reactions; the placeholder's profile ends. Safe to run twice; nothing for another provider.
